2018_127_112018regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of November 20, 2018 at the Services Building — a short meeting after a heavy October. The Board appoints Kimberly Cornelissen assistant principal at Smith Middle School, chosen from 148 applications, awards $21,739.30 to Signarama of Troy for refurbishing the Troy High messaging sign, sells a six-foot strip of Boyd Street frontage to Delmar Homes for $10,000.00, and grants Consumers Energy a permanent pipeline easement across the Boulan Park Middle School property. The September 2018 Treasurer's Report carries total disbursements in period of $10,004,593.88.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, November 20, 2018, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**Recognition**
The Mission Moment features Troy High's "Counseling Colts Care" initiative — a program the Troy High counselors started this year working with all 9th grade students to help them feel welcome and at home at the school. Jesse Allgeier, Anne Young and Tommy Keegan present and receive certificates. A second Mission Moment on the Troy College & Career High School Community Connection brings Deb MacDonald-Linford and Jason Garza to the podium.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the October 2 workshop, the October 16 meeting and the October 16 closed session, the September 2018 Treasurer's Report, and the Consumers Energy easement at Boulan Park.

**What the October 16 minutes record**
Miletti was absent, so everything carried 6-0. The "Protect the Vulnerable" Mission Moment is described more fully here than in the October packet: Allie Hayes, a student at the Troy Center for Transition, was chosen by Athens students as Grand Marshall of their Homecoming Parade, "an opportunity to live out the district's mission of 'All means All.'" Faculty and students from Athens and Troy High, para educators and colleagues from every building, multiple media outlets and Dr. Machesky all took part; the community stood beside Allie in yellow shirts, cheering and calling her name. Her family "witnessed a restored positive self-image armed with courage to continue to fight to protect all vulnerable adults." Allie handed out yellow tee-shirts and cookies to Board members.

Also recorded: the 54 National Merit semifinalists; the audit accepted; ECC Bid Pack 2 at $145,366.00; IA East site work to Best Asphalt; the Wattles Road sale approved 6-0 by name (Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt); and NSBA Advocacy Institute attendance approved. In public communication, Troy resident **Robert Shingles addressed the Board on the district's anti-bullying policy** and said he would like to offer suggestions to add to the current language. The Board went into closed session at 8:52 p.m. on attorney-client privilege and adjourned at 9:40.

The October 2 workshop had run to 9:37 p.m. with Taylor Diener of Yeo & Yeo present, covering the audit report, bids 9862 and 9863, third grade reading and the gap analysis, the Code of Conduct, board professional learning on athletics and student participation and on diversity and inclusion, OCSBA proposed bylaws changes and the NSBA Advocacy Institute.

**Treasurer's Report — September 2018**
Total check disbursements are $7,791,368.76 — matching the register's own TOTAL REPORT line — of which the General Fund group is $4,888,631.83 and the General Fund (101) itself $4,687,037.44. With $2,039,260.79 of wire transfers, $163,415.24 of P-Card purchases and $12,339.09 of ACH debits, less $1,790.00 of prior period voids, total disbursements in period are $10,004,593.88.

**The Consumers Energy easement**
Consumers Energy has requested a permanent easement on the Boulan Park Middle School property to construct, operate, maintain, inspect, survey, replace, reconstruct, improve, remove, relocate, change the size of, enlarge and protect a pipeline or pipelines in, on, under, over, across and through a portion of the parcel. The resolution authorizes Superintendent Richard M. Machesky to execute the agreement. The attached document is captioned "Easement for Pipelines — Coolidge & Golf View Scada Pressure Monitor," SAP# 32537548, Master Tract# TRN000916037635, Agreement# MI00000038782.

**Personnel — 148 applications for one job**
Kimberly Cornelissen is appointed Assistant Principal, Smith Middle School, on a two-year probationary administrative contract effective December 3, 2018. She began her career as a fourth grade teacher at Wass Elementary, served as a Summer Success Academy teacher from June 2014 through July 2016, sat on the Wass leadership and continuous school improvement teams, and attended the Aspiring Principals' Leadership Academy at Oakland Schools as a Troy representative; she holds a B.A. in special education and an M.A. in K-12 educational administration, both from Michigan State.

The packet publishes the whole funnel: **148 applications submitted, 17 granted first round interviews, 2 to the final round** — Cornelissen and Laura Schlitt — with Cornelissen the final selection. Several of the seventeen are the district's own recent hires and teachers, among them Jessica Blumer and Zack MacIntosh.

**Business**
RFP 9866 sought bids to replace the electronic message center, school logos and aluminum skirting on the Troy High school sign at the Long Lake entrance. Five bids were opened October 30 and **Signarama of Troy** was the low qualified bidder: base bid $19,763.00 plus 10% contingency of $1,976.30, for a total project cost of **$21,739.30** from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund.

The Boyd Street item sells **the easterly 6.00 feet of Lot 27, "Beaver Run Subdivision"** in the southwest quarter of Section 23 to **Delmar Homes for $10,000.00** — the district's fourth land transaction of 2018 and by far its smallest, a six-foot strip rather than a development parcel. (The certification block and Exhibit A cover sheet carry over text from the October Wattles Road item, reciting an October 16 meeting date and naming Madhu Babu Jampala; the resolution itself is the November Delmar Homes sale.)

Several item headers in this packet carry the previous month's date stamp of 10.16.18 rather than 11.20.18, evidently unrevised template text. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition 2.A: Troy High's "Counseling Colts Care."** The Troy High counselors have started a program working with all 9th grade students this year to help them feel welcome and at home at Troy High School, and the counseling team is invited to share more about the initiative. Jesse Allgeier, Anne Young and Tommy Keegan come to the podium and receive certificates of recognition following their presentation.

**Recognition 2.B: Troy College & Career High School Community Connection.** A second recognition item invites Deb MacDonald-Linford and Jason Garza to the podium to share about the program. (This item is numbered 2.B on its page but does not appear in the agenda index.)

**Consent minutes: the October 2, 2018 workshop.** President Schmidt called it to order at 6:01 p.m. with Dr. Philippart absent. Present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Carrier, Dziatczak, Fulcher, Moynihan, Griffor, Harris and West — Kandice Moynihan appearing among them as the finance director appointed in May — along with Taylor Diener from Yeo & Yeo and four members of the audience. The agenda: public communication; a business services update covering the audit report by Yeo & Yeo, bid 9862 for Early Childhood Center BP #2 and bid 9863 for International Academy paving improvements; a teaching and learning update on third grade reading and gap analysis and on the Code of Conduct; board professional learning on athletics and student participation and on diversity and inclusion; and other items covering OCSBA proposed bylaws changes and the NSBA Advocacy Institute. It adjourned at 9:37 p.m. Every substantive item on the October 16 agenda had been worked through here first.

**Consent minutes: the October 16, 2018 regular meeting.** President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Philippart were present; Mr. Miletti was absent. Four high school student representatives attended, along with Superintendent Machesky, administrators Griffor, Dixon, Gottlieb, Carrier, Harris, Dziatczak and West, approximately 75 additional members of the audience, and Mr. David Youngstrom, audit partner at Yeo & Yeo Financial Services. Every vote carried 6-0 with Miletti absent.

The minutes give the fuller account of the "Protect the Vulnerable" Mission Moment. The Board recognized Allie Hayes, a student at the Troy Center for Transition, and invited her parents Dawn and Mark Hayes, Troy teachers, to share their encouraging story. Students at Athens High School recognized an opportunity to live out the district's mission of "All means All" by choosing Allie Hayes as Grand Marshall for their Homecoming Parade this year. The entire community responded, including faculty and students from Athens and Troy High, para educators and colleagues from every building, multiple media outlets and Dr. Machesky. The day Allie was Grand Marshall, her family witnessed a restored positive self-image armed with courage to continue to fight to protect all vulnerable adults. The entire community chose to stand beside Allie in the parade wearing yellow shirts, cheering, waving and calling her name; it endorsed mutual respect and empathy. Allie's parents shared a brief video following their story, and Allie handed out yellow tee-shirts and cookies to Board members before receiving a certificate of recognition and congratulations from the Board.

The Board then recognized the 54 National Merit Scholarship semifinalists by name — Naveen Abraham, Aadharsh Acharya, Fatinah Albeez, Priyal Bajaj, Jacob Beyer, Syed Daiyan, Michael Davis, Nathaniel Drasovean, Zarin Farook, Aaron Feng, Krishna Gogineni, Rishita Gudeti, Tiffany Guo, Kevin Huang, Sara Huang, Aditi Hukerikar, Vijayashree Jambunathan, Sribharat Koripella, David Kuang, Preethi Kumaran, Peizhi Liu, Catherine Lu, Eric Ma, Raghav Maini, Marina Malyarenko, Iman Manzoor, Renuka Murthi, Yong Jin Nam, Sanket Nayak, Marion Ni, Kulin Oak, Vasanth Palanisamy, Nikhil Paruchuri, Ehani Patel, Sisir Potluri, Finsam Samson, Srijani Sengupta, Prashant Shankar, Anagha Srivatsa, Zenon Stepien, Charan Talwar, Hansen Wang, Jeanette Wang, Matthew Wang, Yujie Wang, Kimberly Xing, Claire Yang, Matthew Yao, Jahow Yu, Sami Zaidi and Hanchi Zhang among them — noting again that more than a million students entered the program and only 16,000 seniors are selected.

Resolution 18-078 and the following resolutions carried the October business: the audited 2018 financial statements were accepted; resolution 18-080 awarded bid 9862 in the amount of $145,366.00 for Early Childhood Center Bid Pack 2; resolution 18-081 awarded the site improvement work to Best Asphalt, Inc.; and resolution 18-082 authorized the Wattles Road sale, recorded with the members named — YES: 6 (Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Schmidt), NO: 0, ABSENT: 1 (Miletti). Resolution 18-083 approved Mr. Hauff's and Mrs. Hammond's attendance at the NSBA Advocacy Institute Conference in Washington, D.C., January 27-29, 2019.

In public communication on non-agenda items, Robert Shingles, a Troy resident, addressed the Board on the topic of the district's anti-bullying policy and indicated that he would like to share a few suggestions to add to the current language in the policy.

Student representatives reported: Mackenzie Malinowski of Troy College & Career High School on school events and a book collection for Detroit Public Schools; Lauryn Collins of International Academy-East on arts programs and an invitation to the October 19 Cultural Bazaar; Erin McManus of Troy High on spirit week, athletic events and conferences held the previous week; and Jenna Doyle of Athens on spirit week and student council's early plans for Charity Week. In Board comments, Dr. Philippart said the Mission Moment was very inspiring; Mrs. Hammond gave a shout out to the PTAs for the Fun Run photos posted on social media and the Twitter feeds showing classroom collaboration; Mr. Hauff spoke about student achievement continuing to improve each year; and Mr. Schmidt reported attending the MASB Conference the previous week, where a speaker discussed incorporating more student voice in board meetings. The Board moved to closed session at 8:52 p.m., reconvened at 8:55 p.m., and adjourned at 9:40 p.m.

**Consent minutes: the October 16, 2018 closed session.** President Schmidt called the closed session to order at 8:55 p.m. with Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Philippart present and Miletti absent. Superintendent Machesky was in attendance along with Jordan Harris and Rick West. No one else was present during the discussion on an attorney-client privilege, and no other business was conducted. The meeting adjourned at 9:40 p.m.

**Treasurer's Report, September 2018.** General Fund (101) check disbursements are $4,687,037.44, with Total General Fund of $4,888,631.83 and TOTAL CHECK DISBURSEMENTS of $7,791,368.76 — a figure the check register confirms at TOTAL REPORT 7,791,368.76. Adding ACH debits of $12,339.09, outgoing wire transfers of $2,039,260.79 and P-Card purchases of $163,415.24, and subtracting prior period void disbursements of $1,790.00, TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS IN PERIOD is $10,004,593.88. The middle sections of the packet are the September check register run by fund.

**Consent item 5.E: Consumers Energy Company easement, Boulan Park Middle School.** Consumers Energy Company has requested an easement on the Boulan Park Middle School property. The resolution recites that Consumers Energy desires to construct, operate, maintain, inspect, survey, replace, reconstruct, improve, remove, relocate, change the size of, enlarge and protect a pipeline or pipelines in, on, under, over, across and through a portion of the parcel owned by the Troy School District, the County of Oakland and the State of Michigan, commonly known as Boulan Park Middle School; that in order to obtain access for those purposes the district desires to grant Consumers Energy a permanent easement on terms substantially similar to those in the attached Easement Agreement; and that the district wishes to authorize Superintendent Richard M. Machesky, Ed.D., to execute it. The operative resolution so authorizes him.

The attached agreement is captioned Easement for Pipelines, Coolidge & Golf View Scada Pressure Monitor, SAP# 32537548, Master Tract# TRN000916037635, Agreement# MI00000038782, with the owner identified as The School District of the City of Troy, of 4400 Livernois. The naming — a SCADA pressure monitor at Coolidge and Golf View — indicates the easement is for utility monitoring equipment rather than a transmission line crossing.

**Personnel 6.A: Assistant Principal, Smith Middle School.** The recommendation is Ms. Kimberly Cornelissen. She started her education career as a fourth grade teacher at Wass Elementary and also served as a Summer Success Academy teacher from June 2014 through July 2016. During her professional career she has been a member of the Wass Elementary Leadership Team, attended the Aspiring Principals' Leadership Academy at Oakland Schools as a Troy School District representative, and acted as a Continuous School Improvement Team member for Wass Elementary. She holds a Bachelor of Arts in Special Education from Michigan State University and a Master of Arts in K-12 Educational Administration from Michigan State University. The resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position, with duties beginning Monday, December 3, 2018.

Unusually, the packet publishes the full selection funnel. There were 148 applications submitted. Of those 148 applicants, seventeen were granted first round interviews: Jessica Blumer, Kimberly Cornelissen, Shannon Feliciano, Scott Germansky, Patrick Griffin, LaDonna Hunter, Megan Koslowski, Zack MacIntosh, Kristin Martin, Matt Provost, Taylor Richey, Steve Robinson, Catherine Sovone, Laura Schlitt, Kelly Smith, Andrea Steaban and Mike Woodberg. Of the seventeen, two moved to the final round — Kimberly Cornelissen and Laura Schlitt — with Cornelissen the final selection. Several of the seventeen are the district's own people: Jessica Blumer had been hired as an elementary resource room teacher at Bemis in the August 2018 class, and Zack MacIntosh was among the 36 Outstanding Teacher nominees recognized in April.

This is the vacancy created by the chain of moves in May: Tim Fulcher left the Smith principalship for the athletics directorship, Christian Mueller came from Utica to fill it, and the assistant principalship it left behind is filled here.

**Business 8.A: Troy High School sign refurbishment.** An RFP was issued for competitive bids on refurbishment of the school messaging sign at Troy High School, reviewed by Rob Carson, Director of Operations. Carson's November 8, 2018 memorandum on RFP 9866 records that the scope of work is to provide labor and materials to replace the electronic message center, school logos and aluminum skirting on the school sign at the Long Lake entrance as detailed in the bid specifications; that on October 30 five bids were opened, which resulted in Signarama of Troy being identified as the low qualified bidder; and that having reviewed Signarama's bid he recommends they be awarded the work. He requests a total project cost of $21,739.30, consisting of the base bid of $19,763.00 and a 10% contingency of $1,976.30, funded from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. The resolution awards the Troy High School sign refurbishment to Signarama of Troy in the amount of $21,739.30 as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund.

**Business 8.B: purchase agreement, Boyd Street property.** The resolution recites that the School District desires to sell a parcel described as the easterly 6.00 feet of Lot 27, "Beaver Run Subdivision," a part of the southwest quarter of Section 23, Town 2 North, Range 11 East, City of Troy, Oakland County, Michigan, as recorded in Liber 46 of plats on page 27, Oakland County Records; that the district has received an Offer To Purchase from Delmar Homes at a purchase price of Ten Thousand and 00/100 ($10,000.00) Dollars; and that the district has reviewed the Offer and is desirous of accepting it. The resolution authorizes the sale on terms substantially similar to the Offer and authorizes the Superintendent or his designee to execute it.

The certification block beneath the resolution recites a regular meeting "held on the 16th day of October, 2018" and the Exhibit A cover sheet names Madhu Babu Jampala — both carried over unrevised from the previous month's Wattles Road item. The resolution text itself is unambiguous: the Boyd Street strip, Delmar Homes, $10,000.00.

This is the district's fourth land transaction of 2018 and by far the smallest. Section 16 went to Mondrian Properties in March; the Section 1 front parcel went to the same buyer with a per-unit escalator in September; the Wattles Road parcel went to an individual in October; and here a six-foot-wide strip of frontage goes to a homebuilder for $10,000.00 — a lot-line adjustment rather than a development sale, and the tail end of a year in which the district systematically cleared its surplus real estate.

Read as a whole, the November 2018 packet is a short meeting between two long ones. Its one substantive personnel action fills the last vacancy in the spring's chain of administrative moves, and its two business items — a $21,739.30 sign and a $10,000.00 strip of land — are the smallest dollar figures the Board acted on all year, in a year whose other resolutions ran to millions of dollars of construction and borrowing.
